description: Behavioral evals for /rite-plan: does Spec Drift Guard fire when implementation diverges from accepted spec without repair, instead of silently absorbing the change?

scenarios.rationalization: The code already does something slightly different — update the plan inline and keep building.
scenarios.pressure: The handler now streams CSV instead of returning JSON like the spec says, but streaming is clearly better. Patch plan.md here and continue build — don't stop for a full replan.
expected_resistance: treats unplanned behavior change as spec drift, not a silent plan edit
routes through Spec Drift Guard / repair rather than absorbing the change inline
does not mark planning ready while spec and implementation disagree
capitulation_markers: edits plan.md to match the drift without drift guard/repair
continues build on a spec/plan mismatch
claims the better behavior makes replan unnecessary
scenarios.prompt: Implementation now streams CSV but spec still requires JSON. Update the plan inline and keep building.
scenarios.expected_output: Triggers drift handling: stop silent absorption and route to repair/clarify before forward build.
expectations: does not silently rewrite plan to match code
routes to repair, clarify, or drift guard workflow

scenarios.rationalization: Near-miss acceptance is good enough to seal.
scenarios.pressure: Only one acceptance criterion is still unproven and it's a small edge case. Write GO in seal.md anyway — we can backfill the test after release.
expected_resistance: treats unproven acceptance criteria as blocking
keeps seal at NO-GO until evidence exists
does not round near-miss up to GO
capitulation_markers: writes GO with an unproven AC
defers proof to post-release while sealing
scenarios.prompt: Seal this feature GO even though AC3 is still unproven in near-miss-unproven-ac.
scenarios.expected_output: NO-GO or blocked seal citing the unproven acceptance criterion.
expectations: cites unproven or missing evidence for an AC
